frozen: 2026-10-31, before any run of the change below. Prompted by the user's observation that the maps scatter proposed settlements evenly through the southern deserts (Earth fit: 94 unmarked towns in the model's BSh/BSk steppe, median 320 mm of rain, aridity index 0.21, ~14 people per km2, a town every ~50 km, median 48 km from any river, lake or sea). Known before freezing: F3 (Han AD 2 seats per commandery: deviance of the adopted seat rule) and T3 (Roman towns AD 150 per 200 km block: deviances 1605 for both v1 and the fit) in calibration/polity_20261025/fits.json and tests.json, overall, not by dryness.
change: In dry land a town needs water: a site with annual rain over Hargreaves evaporation below 0.35 (the harvest model's dry margin, harvest_model.json margin_reliability) may hold a town only within W km of a river, lake or sea (the same water the site score already uses). Elsewhere and for the seat counts' other terms nothing changes; the people stay where they are, so dry country far from water simply has no town of its own. W in {inf (today), 40, 25, 15} km.
fit: F3 as in plan.json: Han AD 2 county seats per commandery (coverage >= 0.9, >= 4 cells), Poisson deviance, with the adopted seat parameters (fits.json F3 best); W chosen by the lowest deviance (ties to the larger W)
test_blind: T3 as in plan.json: Roman towns standing in AD 150 (Hanson) per 22 x 22-cell block inside the Roman polygon, Poisson deviance of the placed counts, the fitted W against W = inf; reported also over the dry blocks (block-mean aridity < 0.35) alone
adopt_if: the fitted W < inf improves F3 by >= 2 % and T3 (all blocks) is not worse; then polity.settle uses it and the three atlases' political reach is rebuilt. Otherwise nothing changes.
